requirement_text.ISS-0279: Found during WF03-ISS0278-20260822, an ORCH reconciliation audit: GH#324 (ISS-0096) and GH#326 (ISS-0098) were both closed on 2026-08-20 with zero comment and no linked/merged PR in their own GitHub timeline (no closedByPullRequestsReferences, no commit_id on the close event). Contrast with two sibling closures in the same audit (GH#329/ISS-0101 via merged PR #337, GH#357/ISS-0107 via merged PR #437) which both trace cleanly to real fix commits. #324/#326 have no such trail at all -- distinct from the separate ISS-0277/GH#548 finding (three issues closed COMPLETED despite an explicit self-contradicting comment on each): here there is no comment of any kind, so the closure cannot even be checked against its own stated reasoning; it is simply undocumented. On reinvestigation, GH#326 turned out to be genuinely resolvable (this run backfilled it with real R-Co evidence), but GH#324 turned out to still be a real open question (a genuine naming divergence between Letflow and R-Co that this run discovered, not previously known) -- meaning the zero-evidence closure pattern is not even safe as a proxy for the underlying work having happened. Recommend a mechanical gate: gh issue close (or an equivalent local flip to status: resolved/no_defect/instrumented) should require either a --comment citing the resolving evidence, or a genuinely linked/merged PR with a Closes/Fixes reference -- and a periodic audit (or a CI check) should flag any closed issue lacking both.

task.description: ISS-0279 (GH#551, queue task 279) is a PROCESS-GAP issue, not a code defect: GitHub issue/queue-task closures currently carry no mechanical requirement to cite resolving evidence (a comment or a linked/merged PR), so an undocumented, unverifiable closure (as happened for GH#324 and GH#326) is invisible until someone manually reconciles it. Diagnose per WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup -- check docs/issues/ for a prior similar process-gap fix; note the precedent at lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex, a Mix.Task added under ISS-0257/GH#499 as a hard gate wired into the 'letflow.check' alias, which is structurally the same shape of fix: a mechanical lint enforced in CI/local check rather than left to agent diligence) and Step 1 (root cause, not symptom -- this is NOT something to 'reproduce' by running code; the root cause is a missing mechanical enforcement point in two places: (a) WF-03 Step 5 / ISSUE_QUEUE.md's close procedure has no HARD requirement that gh issue close always carries --comment, and (b) nothing audits already-closed issues for evidence after the fact). Do NOT implement the fix yourself. Write a diagnosis identifying: (1) the precise doc locations needing a stated hard requirement (docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md and docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5), (2) the shape of a new mechanical audit tool analogous to letflow.lint_handoffs -- e.g. a new Mix.Task `mix letflow.audit_issue_closures` that shells out to `gh issue list --state closed --json number,comments,closedByPullRequestsReferences,timelineItems` (or equivalent) for issues referenced by docs/issues/*.yaml with a github_issue field, and flags any closed issue with zero comments AND no linked/merged PR reference as a violation, exiting non-zero when new (un-grandfathered) violations exist -- following letflow.lint_handoffs's own grandfather-list pattern so this run does not have to retroactively fix every pre-existing violation (GH#324/GH#326 already resolved by WF03-ISS0278-20260822; anything else historical should be grandfathered, not force-failed). Do NOT decide whether this new task runs against live GitHub in CI (no network) vs. only locally/on-demand -- flag that as an open design question for CODE-DESIGNER to resolve (e.g. it may need to read a locally-cached JSON export, or be documented as a manual/local-only check if CI has no GitHub network access -- check existing CI config for GH network access precedent first). Complete this handoff with your diagnosis in result.summary and next_action: 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design'. Claim by setting status to IN_PROGRESS only.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY LOOKUP: no prior docs/issues/ entry matches this exact symptom (undocumented GitHub issue closures going undetected). Closest precedents, both cited: (1) ISS-0191/lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex -- a Mix.Task auditing handoffs/**/*.json for protocol-required fields, exiting non-zero on new (un-grandfathered) violations; this is the structural template the task.description points at. (2) ISS-0257 (resolved WF03-ISS0257-20260822) -- the precedent for wiring such an existing-but-unenforced audit tool into the 'letflow.check' alias as a HARD gate, including its own worked method for checking in-flight-branch blast radius before hard-gating (gh pr list --state open, diff each against merge-base). No recurrence: this is a new gap, not a fix that failed to hold.

STEP 1 DIAGNOSIS (process-gap, not code defect -- not reproduced by running code, per WF-03's own Step 1 note that a reasoned diagnosis from direct document inspection is the correct method here):

ROOT CAUSE: two missing mechanical enforcement points, both confirmed by direct inspection:
(a) docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md has no close procedure at all -- it only covers issue *filing* (register_task/docs/issues/<ref>.yaml), not closing. docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 (lines 154-181) is the actual close procedure and already requires `gh issue close <n> --comment "..."` with status-branched comment text -- but this is prose instruction only, obeyed at agent discretion. Nothing checks, after the fact, that a closed GitHub issue actually carries that comment or a linked/merged PR. GH#324 and GH#326 were both closed 2026-08-20 with zero comment and no closedByPullRequestsReferences/commit_id -- direct evidence (per ISS-0278.yaml's resolution_note, the discovering run's own findings) that Step 5's prose requirement is not self-enforcing: an agent (or the queue's auto-close-on-Closes/Fixes-keyword path) can close without complying, and nothing flags it until a manual reconciliation audit (WF03-ISS0278-20260822) catches it by chance.
(b) There is no periodic/mechanical audit step anywhere in the pipeline that re-scans already-closed issues for evidence. WF-03 Step 5 is a one-shot, forward-only check (applies only at the moment ISSUE-FIXER closes its own issue) -- it cannot catch closures made outside a WF-03 run (e.g. the queue's own auto-close on a PR's Closes/Fixes reference, per ISS-0278's own note about a possible auto-close mechanism), nor regressions where evidence is later force-edited away.

FIX SHAPE (two surfaces, matching task.description exactly):
1. DOC/PROTOCOL WORDING: WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 (and/or ISSUE_QUEUE.md, which should probably gain its own explicit close-procedure cross-reference/summary since it currently has none) needs upgraded wording from descriptive ('gh issue close <n> --comment ...') to an explicitly stated HARD requirement: a GitHub issue close is only valid if it carries EITHER a --comment citing resolving evidence OR a genuinely linked/merged PR with a Closes/Fixes reference. This closes the prose gap but is still agent-discretion-enforced without (2).
2. NEW AUDIT TOOL: mix letflow.audit_issue_closures (owned_modules already reserves lib/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures.ex), structurally modeled on letflow.lint_handoffs.ex: shells to `gh issue list --state closed --json number,comments,closedByPullRequestsReferences,timelineItems` (or per-issue `gh issue view <n> --json ...`) for every issue referenced by a docs/issues/*.yaml `github_issue` field, flags any closed issue with zero comments AND no linked/merged PR reference as a hard violation, and MUST follow lint_handoffs's own two grandfathering patterns: a `@grandfathered` per-file (per-issue-number) list for already-known pre-existing violations discovered before this tool exists (GH#324/#326 are already resolved by WF03-ISS0278-20260822 so do not need grandfathering by the time this tool lands; CODE-DESIGNER should re-check for any OTHER zero-evidence closures at design/implementation time and grandfather those explicitly, never with a wildcard) -- exits non-zero only on NEW (un-grandfathered) violations, exactly like lint_handoffs's H1-H4/H6 split. Given ISS-0257's own precedent, this should likely also be wired into the `mix letflow.check` alias as a hard gate once its in-flight blast radius is checked the same way ISS-0257 checked it (gh pr list --state open, diff each against merge-base -- but note this new tool's blast radius is EXISTING GITHUB STATE, not open PRs' file changes, so the check needs adapting: run it once standalone first and grandfather whatever it finds, the same principle, different measurement).

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION FLAGGED, NOT RESOLVED HERE: whether mix letflow.audit_issue_closures runs against live GitHub in CI vs. only locally/on-demand. Checked for CI network-access precedent: this repository has NO .github/workflows directory at all (confirmed via Glob) -- 'mix letflow.check' is the enforcement point in place of CI, per ISS-0257's own resolution_note ('this repo's stated convention that mix letflow.check is the enforcement point in place of CI'). So there is no existing CI-with-GitHub-network precedent either way to inherit from; CODE-DESIGNER must decide fresh whether (i) the tool requires `gh` CLI + live network access and is therefore a local/on-demand-only check (documented as such, not wired into any gate assumed to run in a sandboxed/offline environment), or (ii) it reads a locally-cached JSON export refreshed out-of-band, or (iii) some other shape. This question is explicitly NOT resolved by this diagnosis.
